::: {#exm-psrf}
#### Potential scale reduction factor for the Bernoulli sampler

Continuing @exm-burnin,
we compute $\hR$ for the two chains,
first over their first 50 iterations, which include the burn-in,
and then over iterations 501 to 5,000:

```{r}
#| label: psrf
#| code-fold: false
psrf <- function(chains) {
  n <- nrow(chains)
  w <- mean(apply(chains, 2, stats::var))
  b <- n * stats::var(colMeans(chains))
  v_hat <- (n - 1) / n * w + b / n
  sqrt(v_hat / w)
}
chains <- cbind(chain_low, chain_high)
c(
  first_50 = psrf(chains[1:50, ]),
  after_burnin = psrf(chains[501:5000, ])
) |>
  round(3)
```

Here `stats::var(colMeans(chains))` is $\frac{1}{m-1}\sum_j (\bar\theta_j - \bar\theta)^2$,
so `b` is $B$.
While the chains are still approaching the posterior from opposite ends,
$\hR$ is well above 1;
after burn-in it is essentially 1.
:::
